in_hebrew.name: יִדְלֵן
in_hebrew.long_meaning: The wild boar is a fierce and powerful animal. It is a symbol of strength and courage. In the Bible, wild boars are mentioned several times as creatures that inhabit the wilderness and are hunted by the Israelites.

in_greek.name: Ἰδλεὺς
in_greek.long_meaning: The Greek name Ἰδλεὺς (Idleus) is derived from the word 'idō' which means 'to hunt'. The name Wilden, meaning 'wild boar', is a clear reference to the power and strength of this animal.

in_latin.name: Sylvanus
in_latin.long_meaning: The Latin name Sylvanus is derived from the word 'silva' which means 'forest'. It is a name given to the Roman god of the wilderness, woodlands, and forests. While not directly related to the name Wilden, it is a name that shares the same theme of the wild and untamed.

biblical_reference.verse_reference: And Jephthah went through the land, and all Israel was subdued unto him. And Jephthah came to his house at Mizpah: and, behold, his daughter came out to meet him with timbrels and dances: she his only child; beside her he had neither son nor daughter.
biblical_reference.note: This name appears in the Bible as the name of Jephthah's only child, who was a daughter. The name is a reminder of the power and strength of the wild boar, which was a symbol of the power and strength of Jephthah and the Israelites.
